questions.question: The division of labour occurs in:

options.text: neither unicellular nor in multicellular organism

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The division of labour can occur in both unicellular organisms as well as in multicellular organisms.
 
• In unicellular organisms, organelles perform specialized functions, which is a form of division of labour.
 
• In multicellular organisms, different cells, tissues, and organs have specialized functions, leading to a higher level of division of labour.
 
• This specialization increases efficiency and allows organisms to perform complex tasks.
 
• Examples include specialized cells like nerve cells for signal transmission and muscle cells for movement in multicellular organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unicellular Organisms**

 
 
• Examples include bacteria, amoeba, and yeast.
 
• These organisms carry out all life processes within a single cell.
 
 
 
• **Multicellular Organisms**
 
 
• Examples include plants, animals, and fungi.
 
• These organisms have specialized cells that perform different functions, contributing to the overall survival and efficiency of the organism.
 
 
 
• **Cell Specialization**
 
 
• Specialization allows cells to become more efficient in performing specific tasks.
 
• Examples include red blood cells specialized for oxygen transport and white blood cells specialized for immune response.

questions.question: Which cell has changing shapes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An Amoeba is a type of unicellular organism that constantly changes its shape.
 
• This shape-shifting ability is due to the extension and retraction of pseudopodia, which are temporary projections of its cytoplasm.
 
• Pseudopodia are used for movement and capturing food, making the Amoeba highly adaptable in its environment.
 
• The flexibility of its shape allows the Amoeba to navigate through various environments, including water and soil.
 
• Unlike other cells, such as muscle cells or nerve cells, the Amoeba does not have a fixed structure, which is essential for its survival and function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smooth Muscle**

 
 
• Smooth muscle cells have a spindle-shaped structure and are found in the walls of internal organs like the intestines and blood vessels.
 
• They are responsible for involuntary movements and do not change shape like an Amoeba.
 
 
 
• **Ovum**
 
 
• The ovum is a female reproductive cell and has a fixed, spherical shape.
 
• It does not exhibit shape-changing behavior like an Amoeba.
 
 
 
• **Nerve Cell**
 
 
• Nerve cells, or neurons, have a unique structure with long extensions called axons and dendrites to transmit nerve impulses.
 
• They have a stable shape that is crucial for their function in signal transmission, unlike the shape-changing Amoeba.

questions.question: Which of the following lacks membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Viruses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Viruses are acellular entities, meaning they do not have a cellular structure and lack cell membranes.
 
• They are composed of genetic material (either DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein coat called a capsid.
 
• Viruses cannot replicate on their own and must infect a host cell to reproduce.
 
• They do not possess organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, or ribosomes, which are found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Due to their lack of cellular structure, viruses are considered obligate intracellular parasites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plant Cell**

 
 
• Plant cells have a cell wall, a large central vacuole, and chloroplasts in addition to the cell membrane.
 
• These cells are eukaryotic and have membrane-bound organelles.
 
 
 
• **Fungi Cell**
 
 
• Fungi cells are also eukaryotic and have a cell wall made of chitin, in addition to a cell membrane and membrane-bound organelles.
 
 
 
• **Animal Cell**
 
 
• Animal cells lack a cell wall and chloroplasts but have a cell membrane and various membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is/are NOT unicellular?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants are **multicellular organisms**, meaning they are composed of multiple cells that work together to perform various functions.
 
• Each plant cell has a specific role, contributing to the overall structure and function of the plant.
 
• Unlike unicellular organisms, plants have specialized cells for different tasks such as photosynthesis, nutrient transport, and reproduction.
 
• Examples of unicellular organisms include Amoeba, Paramoecium, and Chlamydomonas, which are composed of a single cell that performs all the necessary life functions.
 
• Multicellular organisms like plants have a higher level of organization and complexity compared to unicellular organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amoeba**

 
 
• Amoeba are unicellular organisms that move and ingest food using pseudopodia, which are temporary projections of the cell.
 
• They are commonly found in freshwater environments and play a role in nutrient cycling.
 
 
 
• **Paramoecium**
 
 
• Paramoecium are unicellular organisms that use cilia for movement and feeding.
 
• They are often found in aquatic habitats and are known for their slipper-like shape.
 
 
 
• **Chlamydomonas**
 
 
• Chlamydomonas are unicellular green algae that have flagella for movement and are capable of photosynthesis.
 
• They serve as a model organism in biological research due to their simple structure and ease of cultivation.

questions.question: Who coined the term ‘protoplasm’ for the fluid substance of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purkinje**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **‘protoplasm’** was coined by the Czech physiologist **Jan Evangelista Purkinje**.
 
• Purkinje introduced the term in 1839 while studying the embryonic development of chickens.
 
• Protoplasm refers to the living content of a cell that is surrounded by a plasma membrane.
 
• It is composed mainly of water, proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and inorganic salts.
 
• The concept of protoplasm has evolved, and it is now generally referred to as the cytoplasm and nucleoplasm within eukaryotic cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virchow**

 
 
• Rudolf Virchow was a German pathologist known for his advancement of the cell theory.
 
• He introduced the concept that all cells arise from pre-existing cells, encapsulated in the Latin phrase "Omnis cellula e cellula".
 
 
 
• **Robert Brown**
 
 
• Robert Brown was a Scottish botanist who discovered the cell nucleus in 1831.
 
• His contributions to botany include the detailed study of plant pollination mechanisms and the random movement of particles in fluid, known as Brownian motion.
 
 
 
• **Robert Hooke**
 
 
• Robert Hooke was an English scientist who is credited with the discovery of the cell.
 
• In 1665, he published "Micrographia", where he detailed his observations of cork cells using a microscope.

questions.question: Which organelle is found ONLY in plant cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

**Note: **The correct answer as per the official answer key is **Mitochondria** but in actual the correct answer would be **chloroplast** as they are only found in plant cells which allows plants to produce their own food using sunlight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells and certain algae, and they are not present in animal cells.
 
• They are responsible for photosynthesis, a process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• Chloroplasts contain the pigment chlorophyll, which captures light energy.
 
• These organelles have their own DNA and replicate independently of the cell.
 
• Chloroplasts have a double membrane structure with an inner network of thylakoid membranes where the light reactions of photosynthesis occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Known as the powerhouses of the cell, they generate most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration.
 
• Present in both plant and animal cells.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• These are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• Lysosomes are generally found in animal cells. They are found in plant cells in some rare conditions.
 
• They are often referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell because they help in the degradation of macromolecules.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• It is a network of membranes within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells, involved in protein and lipid synthesis.
 
• The ER is divided into two types: rough ER (with ribosomes) and smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and folding, while smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

questions.question: Which cell organelle serves as a channel for transport of material between various regions of cytoplasm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endoplasmic reticulum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) serves as a **channel for the transport of materials** between various regions of the cytoplasm.
 
• The ER is an extensive network of membranes found throughout the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It is divided into two regions: the **rough ER** (which has ribosomes attached to its surface) and the **smooth ER** (which lacks ribosomes).
 
• The rough ER is primarily involved in the synthesis and processing of proteins, while the smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification.
 
• The ER is crucial for the **transport and modification of proteins** that are either secreted by the cell or incorporated into the cell membrane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Known as the powerhouses of the cell, they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They have a double-membrane structure and their own DNA and ribosomes.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• These membrane-bound organelles contain enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• Referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell, they help degrade macromolecules.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast**
 
 
• These organelles are found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae and conduct photosynthesis.
 
• They capture light energy and convert it into chemical energy in the form of glucose through photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules acts as an information source for making proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deoxyribonucleic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) serves as the primary information source for making proteins in the cell.
 
• DNA contains the genetic instructions necessary for the development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.
 
• The sequences of nucleotides in DNA are transcribed into messenger RNA (mRNA) which is then translated into protein by ribosomes.
 
• DNA is composed of two strands that coil around each other to form a double helix, carrying the genetic instructions.
 
• DNA replication is essential for cell division, ensuring that each new cell receives an exact copy of the DNA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribonucleic acid (RNA)**

 
 
• RNA is involved in various roles such as coding, decoding, regulation, and expression of genes.
 
• Messenger RNA (mRNA) conveys genetic information from DNA to the ribosome, where it directs protein synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Proteins**
 
 
• Proteins are large, complex molecules that play many critical roles in the body, such as catalyzing metabolic reactions and DNA replication.
 
• They are made up of amino acids and are essential for the structure, function, and regulation of the body's tissues and organs.
 
 
 
• **Genes**
 
 
• Genes are segments of DNA that carry hereditary information and are responsible for guiding the process of creating proteins.
 
• Each gene provides instructions for making a specific protein or set of proteins.

• It is a network of membranes within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells, involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following is the longest cell in our body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nerve cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nerve cells, also known as neurons, are the longest cells in the human body.
 
• Neurons are specialized for the transmission of electrical impulses throughout the body.
 
• Each neuron consists of a cell body, dendrites, and an axon, with the axon being the long, thread-like part that transmits impulses away from the cell body.
 
• Neurons play a crucial role in the nervous system by enabling communication between different parts of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ovum**

 
 
• The ovum, or egg cell, is one of the largest cells in the human body, but not the longest.
 
• It is a reproductive cell that, when fertilized by a sperm cell, can develop into a new organism.
 
 
 
• **Blood Cells**
 
 
• Blood cells include red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets.
 
• RBCs are responsible for oxygen transport, WBCs for immune response, and platelets for blood clotting.
 
 
 
• **Fat Cells**
 
 
• Fat cells, or adipocytes, are specialized for the storage of fat and are important for energy regulation.
 
• They play a role in cushioning and insulating the body.

questions.question: Where does the following reaction take place in a cell? The breakdown of glucose, a six-carbon molecule, into a three-carbon molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In the cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The breakdown of glucose into a three-carbon molecule, known as glycolysis, takes place in the cytoplasm.
 
• Glycolysis is the first step in cellular respiration and does not require oxygen (anaerobic process).
 
• During glycolysis, one molecule of glucose (a six-carbon molecule) is converted into two molecules of pyruvate (a three-carbon molecule).
 
• This process produces a small amount of ATP and NADH, which are used as energy carriers in the cell.
 
• The pyruvate produced in glycolysis can further enter the mitochondria for the citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle) if oxygen is available.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Often referred to as the powerhouses of the cell, mitochondria are responsible for the production of ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• They have a double-membrane structure, with the inner membrane forming folds known as cristae to increase the surface area for ATP production.
 
• Mitochondria contain their own DNA and ribosomes, indicating their evolutionary origin from free-living prokaryotes.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus is involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It consists of a series of flattened membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus**
 
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, housing the cell's genetic material (DNA).
 
• It is surrounded by a double membrane called the nuclear envelope, which contains nuclear pores for the exchange of materials between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.question: What are the basic building units of organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Cells are the basic structural and functional units of all living organisms.
 
• They can exist as independent single-celled organisms or as part of a multicellular organism.
 
• Cells carry out essential processes such as metabolism, energy conversion, and reproduction.
 
• There are two main types of cells: prokaryotic cells, which do not have a defined nucleus, and eukaryotic cells, which have a defined nucleus and organelles.
 
• Cells are composed of various organelles that perform specific functions necessary for the cell's survival and proper functioning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tissues**

 
 
• Tissues are groups of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.
 
• There are four basic types of tissues in animals: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues.
 
 
 
• **Organs**
 
 
• Organs are structures made up of different types of tissues that work together to perform specific functions within an organism.
 
• Examples include the heart, lungs, and brain in animals, and roots, stems, and leaves in plants.
 
 
 
• **Organ Systems**
 
 
• Organ systems are groups of organs that work together to perform complex functions necessary for the survival of the organism.
 
• Examples of organ systems in animals include the circulatory system, respiratory system, and digestive system.

questions.question: Name the scientist who first discovered the cell in 1665.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Robert Hooke was the first scientist to discover cells in 1665.
 
• He made this discovery while observing a thin slice of cork under a microscope.
 
• Hooke coined the term "cell" because the cork cells reminded him of the cells (small rooms) in a monastery.
 
• This discovery was published in his book "Micrographia".
 
• Hooke's work laid the foundation for the development of cell theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Matthias Jakob Schleiden**

 
 
• He was a German botanist who co-founded the cell theory.
 
• Schleiden proposed that all plants are made of cells.
 
 
 
• **Theodor Schwann**
 
 
• He was a German physiologist who also co-founded the cell theory.
 
• Schwann extended the cell theory to animals, proposing that all living things are composed of cells.
 
 
 
• **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek**
 
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of Microbiology".
 
• Van Leeuwenhoek was the first to observe and describe single-celled organisms (protozoa and bacteria) using a microscope.

questions.question: Which of the following substances can move across the cell membrane by diffusion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Diffusion is a passive transport mechanism where substances move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• Oxygen is a small, nonpolar molecule that can easily diffuse across the cell membrane without the need for transport proteins.
 
• Nucleic acids, proteins, and starch are large molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane by simple diffusion.
 
• The cell membrane is selectively permeable, allowing only certain molecules to pass through while blocking others.
 
• Oxygen diffusion is crucial for cellular respiration, a process that generates ATP, the energy currency of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Facilitated Diffusion**

 
 
• This process involves the use of transport proteins to move substances across the cell membrane.
 
• It is used for molecules that cannot diffuse directly through the lipid bilayer, such as glucose and amino acids.
 
 
 
• **Active Transport**
 
 
• Active transport requires energy in the form of ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient.
 
• This process involves transport proteins such as pumps and is essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Endocytosis and Exocytosis**
 
 
• These are processes used by cells to transport large molecules or particles across the cell membrane.
 
• Endocytosis involves the engulfing of substances into the cell, while exocytosis involves the expulsion of substances from the cell.

questions.question: The full form of SER, a cell organelle, which helps in the manufacture of fat molecules, or lipids, important for cell function is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is involved in the synthesis of lipids, including phospholipids and steroids.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the metabolism of carbohydrates and detoxification of drugs and poisons.
 
• SER also helps in the storage of calcium ions which are important for muscle contraction.

questions.question: Which process ensures half the amount of DNA in reproductive cells as compared to non-reproductive cells?

__
 
• **Meiosis** is the process that results in gametes (sperm and egg cells) having half the amount of DNA compared to somatic (body) cells.
 
• It consists of two consecutive cell divisions, known as Meiosis I and Meiosis II, without an intervening round of DNA replication.
 
• This reduction is crucial for maintaining the constant chromosome number across generations when gametes fuse during fertilization.
 
• Meiosis introduces genetic diversity through the processes of crossing over and independent assortment of chromosomes.

• **Haploid Cells**
 
 
• Cells that contain one set of chromosomes (n), such as gametes, resulting from Meiosis.

• The fusion of a haploid sperm cell with a haploid egg cell to form a diploid zygote.

questions.question: What will happen when a plant cell is put in a medium having higher water concentration than the cell?

options.text: It will not show any change

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It will likely swell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **plant cell** is placed in a medium with higher water concentration (hypotonic solution) than the cell, water enters the cell due to **osmosis**.
 
• **Osmosis** is the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a **semi-permeable membrane**.
 
• Plant cells have a **rigid cell wall** that prevents them from bursting under osmotic pressure.
 
• The entry of water into the cell causes the **vacuole** to expand, pushing the cell membrane against the cell wall, leading to the cell swelling.
 
• The pressure exerted by the swollen vacuole against the cell wall is called **turgor pressure**, which helps maintain the shape and rigidity of the cell.
 
• This swelling is critical for the plant's **structural integrity and physiological processes**, such as nutrient transport and photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It will not show any change**__

 __
 
• This would occur if the plant cell was placed in an **isotonic solution**, where the concentration of water is the same inside and outside the cell.
 
• No net movement of water occurs, and the cell remains unchanged.
 
 
 
• **It will likely shrink**__
 __
 
• This happens when the plant cell is placed in a **hypertonic solution**, where the water concentration outside the cell is lower than inside.
 
• Water moves out of the cell, causing the cell to lose turgor pressure and shrink, a process known as **plasmolysis**.

• Plant cells do not burst due to the presence of a **rigid cell wall**, which can withstand high internal pressure.

questions.question: An organism simply splits into two equal halves during cell division. What is it known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a type of asexual reproduction common among prokaryotes such as bacteria.
 
• In binary fission, an organism duplicates its genetic material and then divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.
 
• This process ensures that each daughter cell receives a copy of the parent organism's genetic material.
 
• Binary fission is efficient and allows for rapid population growth, especially in favorable environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regeneration**

 
 
• Regeneration is the process by which certain organisms can regrow lost or damaged parts of their body.
 
• Examples include the regrowth of limbs in starfish or tails in lizards.
 
• This is different from binary fission as it involves repairing or replacing damaged structures rather than creating new organisms.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• Budding is another form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• It is commonly observed in yeast and some invertebrates like hydra.
 
• Unlike binary fission, budding results in the formation of a new organism while the parent organism remains.
 
 
 
• **Spore formation**
 
 
• Spore formation is a method of asexual reproduction that involves the formation of spores by the parent organism.
 
• These spores are typically resistant to extreme conditions and can remain dormant for long periods.
 
• When conditions become favorable, spores germinate to form new organisms.
 
• This is a common reproductive strategy among fungi and some bacteria.
